definition.def: Your reaction to something that has happened or something that you have experienced is what you feel, say, or do because of it.
examples: Reaction to the visit is mixed. [+ to]
The initial reaction of most participants is fear.
He was surprised that his answer should have caused such a strong reaction.

definition.def: A reaction against something is a way of behaving or doing something that is deliberately different from what has been done before.
examples: All new fashion starts out as a reaction against existing convention. [+ against]
Her three years of freedom seemed like a reaction against that childhood.

definition.def: If there is a reaction against something, it becomes unpopular.
examples: Premature moves in this respect might well provoke a reaction against the reform. [+ against]
The idealism may be a reaction against the failure of society to manage itself.

definition.def: Your reactions are your ability to move quickly in response to something, for example when you are in danger.
examples: If his reactions are so slow, he shouldn't be in charge of a bus.
The sport requires very fast reactions.

definition.def: Reaction is the belief that the political or social system of your country should not change. [disapproval]
examples: Thus, he aided reaction and thwarted progress.
...their victory against the forces of reaction and censorship.

definition.def: A chemical reaction is a process in which two substances combine together chemically to form another substance.
examples: Ozone is produced by the reaction between oxygen and ultra-violet light.
Catalysts are materials which greatly speed up chemical reactions.

definition.def: If you have a reaction to a substance such as a drug, or to something you have touched, you are affected unpleasantly or made ill by it.
examples: Every year, 5000 people have life-threatening reactions to anaesthetics. [+ to]
Common foods which cause this kind of reaction are fish, eggs, and shellfish.

examples.sentence: The Coach brand had been a symbol of opulence and luxury for nearly 70 years, and the most obvious reaction to the downturn would have been to lower prices.
In reaction to the backward discharge of bullets, the gun, and hence the boat, move forwards.

However, it wasn't until the discovery of the reaction principle, which was the key to space travel and so represents one of the great milestones in the history of scientific thought, that rocket technology was able to develop.
The reason is that nobody associated the reaction principle with the idea of travelling through space to a neighbouring world.
The reaction to the ejection of these small particles causes the rocket to move forwards.
There is evidence that the reaction principle was applied practically well before the rocket was invented.
The reaction to the discharging steam provided the bird with motive power.
Nevertheless, the modern day space programs owe their success to the humble beginnings of those in previous centuries who developed the foundations of the reaction principle.

In purely scientific terms, Baekeland's major contribution to the field is not so much the actual discovery of the material to which he gave his name, but rather the method by which a reaction between phenol and formaldehyde could be controlled, thus making possible its preparation on a commercial basis.

Other substances were then introduced: including fillers, such as woodflour, asbestos or cotton, which increase strength and moisture resistance, catalysts (substances to speed up the reaction between two chemicals without joining to either) and hexa, a compound of ammonia and formaldehyde which supplied the additional formaldehyde necessary to form a thermosetting resin.
